name: Florence completes third circle
summary: In the 1280s and 1290s, the Florentine commune undertakes its third and final circuit of city walls, enclosing an area of approximately 630 hectares, far larger than the actual built-up city, to accommodate anticipated growth. The walls are nearly 9 kilometers in circumference with 73 towers and 15 gates. Construction is funded by the Parte Guelfa (the Guelf merchant faction). These walls, completed by the 1330s, define Florence's urban footprint for 600 years. The investment signals Florence's extraordinary economic confidence: it is building walls for a city twice its current size.

_quarry.structural_significance: The third circuit of walls defines Florence's urban geography until the 19th century; the massive investment signals the extraordinary wealth generated by Florentine banking and wool; the walls protect the city during the Italian Wars of the 14th–15th centuries
